idiom_name: structural interface Message<H, B> with a literal discriminant; Web Headers; CloudEvents types
implementation_notes: Structural typing means the pattern is a type declaration rather than an implementation: interface Message<H, B> { headers: H; body: B } (or a discriminated union keyed by a literal type field) describes the package, and JSON.parse/JSON.stringify with a schema check at the boundary is the serialization. At runtime the platform's Headers interface (used by Request/Response) is the metadata section, and standards such as CloudEvents give the header vocabulary concrete names - required context attributes specversion, type, source and id plus a data payload - with published TypeScript types, so messages interoperate with third-party tooling. A class is justified only when header invariants must be enforced or the body is binary (ArrayBuffer/Blob/stream).
pitfalls: Types are erased: a JSON.parse result is any/unknown and nothing validates the header or body shape at runtime, so without a schema (zod, JSON Schema, type guard) the contract exists only in the compiler.
HTTP header names are case-insensitive on the wire but object keys are not: mixing 'X-Correlation-Id' and 'x-correlation-id' produces two entries that intermediaries may treat as different fields.
BigInt, Date, Map and Buffer do not survive JSON.stringify (a Buffer becomes {type:'Buffer',data:[...]}), so the body's wire encoding must be stated in the contract and applied explicitly.
